title: Metabolic response to sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition in type 2 diabetic patients
authors: Ferrannini E, Muscelli E, Frascerra S, Baldi S, Mari A, Heise T, et al.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, age 62 ± 7 years, BMI 31.6 ± 4.6 kg/m2, HbA1c 55 ± 8 mmol/mol, at the University of Pisa and Profil
funder: This study was funded by Boehringer Ingelheim. This study was sponsored by Boehringer Ingelheim; two authors, Uli C. Broedl and Hans-Juergen Woerle, are employees of Boehringer Ingelheim.
authorConflicts: Ferrannini has served as an ad hoc consultant and occasional speaker for Boehringer Ingelheim, Merck, Sanofi, Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson, Astellas, Daiichi Sankyo, Bristol-Myers Squibb/AstraZeneca and Novartis; Mari has received research grants from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk; Heise is an employee of Profil; Broedl and Woerle are employees of Boehringer Ingelheim.
result: Open-label, single-arm: baseline, a single 25 mg dose of empagliflozin and 4 weeks of 25 mg daily, each with a mixed meal, dual glucose tracers and indirect calorimetry. After the first dose, urinary glucose was 8 g over 3 h of fasting and 29 g over 5 h after the meal; glycaemia after 3 h of fasting fell by 2.2 ± 0.9 mmol/L against 0.9 ± 0.7 mmol/L at baseline, and fasting endogenous glucose production rose by about 30%. After the meal the insulin response fell and the glucagon response rose. After 4 weeks the fall in glucose oxidation was matched by a rise in lipid oxidation.
